exam.title: Statistics - Advanced Exam
exam.subtitle: Probability Theory and Inferential Statistics
exam.instructions: Complete all tasks thoroughly. Always show your solution approach. Permitted aids: non-programmable calculator, standard normal distribution and t-distribution tables.

exercises.title: Medical Test
exercises.description:
A rare disease occurs in the population with a prevalence of 0.2%. A test for this disease has a sensitivity of 95% and a specificity of 98%.

a) What is the probability that a randomly selected person tests positive?
b) What is the probability that a person with a positive test result is actually sick?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Define events
Let D = 'person is sick', T+ = 'test is positive'
Given: P(D) = 0.002, P(T+|D) = 0.95, P(T-|D^c) = 0.98
Therefore: P(D^c) = 0.998, P(T+|D^c) = 0.02

Step 3: Part b) - Bayes' theorem
$P(D|T+) = \frac{P(T+|D) \cdot P(D)}{P(T+)}$
$P(D|T+) = \frac{0.95 \cdot 0.002}{0.02186} = \frac{0.0019}{0.02186} \approx 0.0869$

Step 4: Interpretation
a) The probability of a positive test is about 2.19%
b) Despite a positive test, the probability of actually being sick is only about 8.69%
This shows the importance of prior probability for rare diseases.

exercises.title: Binomial and Poisson Distribution
exercises.description:
In a production line, electronic components are manufactured. The probability of a defective component is p = 0.03.

a) What is the probability that exactly 2 out of 50 components are defective?
b) Approximate this probability using the Poisson distribution.
c) How many components must be produced at minimum so that with probability at least 90%, at least one defective component is included?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Part a) - Binomial distribution
X ~ B(50; 0.03), sought: P(X = 2)
$P(X = 2) = \binom{50}{2} \cdot 0.03^2 \cdot 0.97^{48}$
P(X = 2) = 1225 · 0.0009 · 0.2371 ≈ 0.2611

Step 2: Part b) - Poisson approximation
λ = n · p = 50 · 0.03 = 1.5
$Y \sim \text{Pois}(1.5), \quad P(Y = 2) = \frac{e^{-1.5} \cdot 1.5^2}{2!}$
$P(Y = 2) = \frac{0.2231 \cdot 2.25}{2} \approx 0.2510$

Step 3: Comparison of approximation
Exact value: 0.2611
Poisson approximation: 0.2510
$\text{Relative error: } \frac{|0.2611 - 0.2510|}{0.2611} \approx 3.9\%$
The approximation is very good.

Step 4: Part c) - Calculate minimum number
Sought: smallest n with P(X ≥ 1) ≥ 0.9
P(X ≥ 1) = 1 - P(X = 0) = 1 - 0.97^n ≥ 0.9
0.97^n ≤ 0.1
n · ln(0.97) ≤ ln(0.1)
$n \geq \frac{\ln(0.1)}{\ln(0.97)} = \frac{-2.303}{-0.0305} \approx 75.5$

Step 5: Answer part c)
At least n = 76 components must be produced.
Verification: P(X ≥ 1) = 1 - 0.97^76 ≈ 1 - 0.0993 ≈ 0.9007 > 0.9 ✓

exercises.title: Normal Distribution and Standardization
exercises.description:
The height of men is normally distributed with μ = 175 cm and σ = 8 cm.

a) What is the proportion of men who are between 170 cm and 185 cm tall?
b) Determine the 95% quantile of height.
c) In a group of 20 men: What is the probability that at most 3 are taller than 180 cm?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Distribution and standardization
$X \sim N(175, 8^2)$, standardization: $Z = \frac{X - 175}{8}$
Z ~ N(0,1) is standard normal

Step 3: Part b) - 95% quantile
Sought: x₀.₉₅ with P(X ≤ x₀.₉₅) = 0.95
From table: Φ(1.645) = 0.95, so z₀.₉₅ = 1.645
x₀.₉₅ = μ + z₀.₉₅ · σ = 175 + 1.645 · 8 = 175 + 13.16 = 188.16 cm

Step 4: Part c) - Binomial distribution of the group
$\text{First: } P(X > 180) = P\left(Z > \frac{180-175}{8}\right) = P(Z > 0.625)$
= 1 - Φ(0.625) = 1 - 0.7340 = 0.2660
Let Y = number of men > 180 cm in group of 20
Y ~ B(20; 0.2660)

exercises.title: Confidence Intervals
exercises.description:
To estimate the average waiting time at a bus stop, a sample of n = 25 measurements was taken. The sample mean is x̄ = 8.4 minutes with a sample standard deviation of s = 2.1 minutes.

a) Determine a 95% confidence interval for the true average waiting time.
b) How large would the sample size need to be so that the width of the 95% confidence interval is at most 1 minute?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Prerequisites and distribution
Sample size: n = 25
Sample mean: x̄ = 8.4
Sample standard deviation: s = 2.1
Since σ unknown and n < 30, we use t-distribution with df = n-1 = 24

Step 2: Part a) - 95% confidence interval
$\text{Confidence interval: } \bar{x} \pm t_{0.975;24} \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$
From t-table: t₀.₉₇₅;₂₄ = 2.064
$\text{Standard error: } SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{2.1}{\sqrt{25}} = \frac{2.1}{5} = 0.42$

Step 3: Calculation of confidence interval
Margin of error: E = 2.064 · 0.42 = 0.867
Confidence interval: [8.4 - 0.867; 8.4 + 0.867] = [7.533; 9.267]
Interpretation: With 95% confidence, the true average waiting time is between 7.53 and 9.27 minutes.

Step 4: Part b) - Required sample size
$\text{Width of CI} = 2E = 2 \cdot t_{0.975;n-1} \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} \leq 1$
$\text{Thus: } t_{0.975;n-1} \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} \leq 0.5$
For large n: t₀.₉₇₅;ₙ₋₁ ≈ 1.96
$1.96 \cdot \frac{2.1}{\sqrt{n}} \leq 0.5$

Step 5: Solve for n
$\frac{1.96 \cdot 2.1}{\sqrt{n}} \leq 0.5$
$\sqrt{n} \geq \frac{1.96 \cdot 2.1}{0.5} = \frac{4.116}{0.5} = 8.232$
n ≥ 67.76
At least n = 68 observations are needed.

exercises.title: t-Test for the Mean
exercises.description:
A pharmaceutical company claims that a new drug reduces the healing time of a disease to an average of μ = 12 days. In a clinical study with n = 16 patients, the average healing time was x̄ = 13.5 days with a standard deviation of s = 3.2 days.

Test at the 5% level whether the drug is less effective than claimed.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Formulate hypotheses
H₀: μ = 12 days (drug is as effective as claimed)
H₁: μ > 12 days (drug is less effective)
One-sided test, significance level α = 0.05

Step 2: Determine test statistic
Since σ unknown and n = 16 < 30, we use t-test
$\text{Test statistic: } t = \frac{\bar{x} - \mu_0}{s/\sqrt{n}} = \frac{13.5 - 12}{3.2/\sqrt{16}} = \frac{1.5}{3.2/4} = \frac{1.5}{0.8} = 1.875$
Degrees of freedom: df = n - 1 = 15

Step 3: Determine critical value
For one-sided test with α = 0.05 and df = 15:
Critical value: t₀.₀₅;₁₅ = 1.753
Rejection region: t > 1.753

Step 4: Test decision
Observed test statistic: t = 1.875
Critical value: t₀.₀₅;₁₅ = 1.753
Since 1.875 > 1.753, t lies in the rejection region
⇒ H₀ is rejected at the 5% level

Step 5: Calculate p-value
p-value = P(T₁₅ > 1.875)
From t-table: P(T₁₅ > 1.875) lies between 0.025 and 0.05
More precisely: p-value ≈ 0.04
Since p-value < α = 0.05, this confirms the rejection of H₀

Step 6: Conclusion
At the 5% significance level, there is sufficient evidence that the drug is less effective than claimed. The average healing time is significantly longer than 12 days.

exercises.title: Linear Regression
exercises.description:
An automobile manufacturer investigates the relationship between engine power (x, in HP) and fuel consumption (y, in l/100km). The following data were collected:

Σx = 1200, Σy = 72, Σx² = 156000, Σy² = 576, Σxy = 9360, n = 10

a) Calculate the regression line y = a + bx.
b) Interpret the regression coefficient b.
c) Calculate the correlation coefficient r.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Calculate means
$\bar{x} = \frac{\Sigma x}{n} = \frac{1200}{10} = 120$
$\bar{y} = \frac{\Sigma y}{n} = \frac{72}{10} = 7.2$

Step 2: Calculate auxiliary values for regression
$S_{xx} = \Sigma x^2 - n\bar{x}^2 = 156000 - 10 \cdot 120^2 = 156000 - 144000 = 12000$
$S_{yy} = \Sigma y^2 - n\bar{y}^2 = 576 - 10 \cdot 7.2^2 = 576 - 518.4 = 57.6$
$S_{xy} = \Sigma xy - n\bar{x}\bar{y} = 9360 - 10 \cdot 120 \cdot 7.2 = 9360 - 8640 = 720$

Step 3: Part a) - Regression coefficients
$\text{Slope: } b = \frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}} = \frac{720}{12000} = 0.06$
$\text{Intercept: } a = \bar{y} - b\bar{x} = 7.2 - 0.06 \cdot 120 = 7.2 - 7.2 = 0$
Regression line: y = 0 + 0.06x = 0.06x

Step 4: Part b) - Interpretation of b
The regression coefficient b = 0.06 means:
When engine power increases by 1 HP, fuel consumption increases on average by 0.06 l/100km.
This corresponds to an increase of 6 l/100km per 100 HP additional power.

Step 5: Part c) - Correlation coefficient
$r = \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}} = \frac{720}{\sqrt{12000 \cdot 57.6}} = \frac{720}{\sqrt{691200}} = \frac{720}{831.4} \approx 0.866$

Step 6: Interpretation of correlation
The correlation coefficient r = 0.866 shows a strong positive linear relationship between engine power and fuel consumption.
About 75% of the variance in fuel consumption (r² = 0.75) is explained by engine power.
